ecosystem.notes: Bookings is a non-GAAP measure (sales of Robux and subscriptions, before deferral). Roblox records revenue gross, as principal, so Revenue includes the money later paid to developers; developer exchange fees are an expense line, recognised 'as earned Robux are accumulated by creators that are qualified and registered in the Developer Exchange Program'. Revenue / Bookings therefore overstates what Roblox keeps. Developer exchange fees are the expense recognised in 2025, not necessarily cash paid in 2025.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Roblox records revenue gross, so revenue already includes amounts later paid to developers; the share would understate what creators receive.

footprint.notes: Roblox reports DAUs, hours engaged and bookings by region (US and Canada, Europe, APAC, Rest of world), but in the FY2025 10-K the regional values appear only inside chart images (as in the FY2024 10-K and its Q4 2024 Supplemental Materials, checked last edition; the FY2025 supplemental materials were not re-checked). Those chart values were not transcribed, because a quote must be text in the document. The one text-verifiable regional user figure is the FY2025 10-K's 'approximately 82% of our DAUs ... derived from outside the U.S. and Canada region' (year ended Dec 31, 2025). Property and equipment, net by geography is at Dec 31, 2025 (U.S. $762.2 million, rest of world $122.6 million). The 10-K says over 200 of its 3,065 full-time employees were outside the U.S.; no country split is given. The 10-K describes 25 regional data centers across North America, South America, Asia-Pacific and Europe without naming or sizing them individually, so they are not sites. Besides the new headquarters, Roblox still leases about 427,271 sq ft at its prior San Mateo headquarters, partly sub-leased. Revenue by region is in the records and not repeated.
